note: Diarization changes its mind after alerts have already fired (DR-014, DR-022). Exercises the whole lifecycle: fire, withdraw, update, and withdraw again on PENDING. Withdrawing an alert is the honest behaviour - quietly misattributing a quote is the thing this project exists to prevent.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Before we go further, do you want the premium support plan?

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: No, I don't need the premium plan. We've never used support in three years.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Understood, I'll leave it off the quote.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: So obviously we need the premium plan on this one, that's a given.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: And Friday is a hard deadline, Monday won't work.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: So Monday delivery works for you?

events.speaker: B
events.text: does not want the premium plan

revisions.why: u3 was actually the agent speaking, not the customer. Two people disagreeing is not one person contradicting themselves, so the alert must go.
u6 belongs to a third participant. Commitment drift makes no same-speaker claim, so the alert survives with corrected attribution.
Diarization backs off to PENDING. A conflict cannot be attributed to nobody, so an already-updated alert is withdrawn in turn.
